text:
B: Hello. Can you hear me?
A: Yeah. Hiya.
B: Gareth.
A: Bianca.
B: Where are you, then?
A: Wolverhampton. Bilston, kind of.
B: Walthamstow, me. London.
A: Oh right.
B: So what d'you do?
A: Erm, I'm at uni. Second year, Accounting and Finance.
B: Right. Do you like it?
A: It's alright. I didn't pick it 'cause I love it, like. It pays, and accountants don't really get made redundant, do you know what I mean. I want a placement year at a firm in Birmingham next year, then do my ACCA.
B: That's more of a plan than I had at twenty.
A: What do you do?
B: Structural engineer. Er, I check buildings won't fall down, basically. Loft conversions, refurbs, that sort of thing.
A: Oh. Do you like that?
B: Mostly. The engineering bit's fine. It's the paperwork I can't stand. My timesheets are always late. Every month someone from finance chases me, and every month I say I'll do them on Friday, and then it's Tuesday.
A: That'd be me chasing you, then. In a few years.
B: Probably, yeah. Go easy.
A: I won't lol.
B: Fair enough. Er, what's Wolverhampton like? Never been.
A: It's fine. Nothing special. My boyfriend's obsessed with Wolves, so I end up watching the highlights.
B: Palace, me. So I sympathise with both of you.
A: I couldn't name like, more than three players, to be honest.
B: That's probably healthier.
A: Mm.
B: You live in Bilston with him, then?
A: Yeah, flat above some shops. It was cheaper than us both living at home, so.
B: Romantic.
A: It's kind of practical more than romantic, yeah.
B: I'm renting on my own. Landlord's been promising to fix the extractor fan in the bathroom for two years.
A: Two years? Ours took like a week for the boiler. I just kept ringing them till they sent someone. Every day, same time. They give up in the end.
B: Maybe I should get you to ring mine.
A: Give it me, I'll do it.
B: Ha. I might take you up on that. What're you doing for fun, then, when you're not doing accounts?
A: Erm, gym, TV. Crime stuff mostly. Reality shows.
B: Which crime stuff?
A: Whatever's on Netflix. I just finished one about a nurse, I can't remember what it's called.
B: I read the odd book about bridges collapsing. Same idea, I suppose.
A: That sounds kind of grim.
B: It's fascinating, honestly. Usually it's one bloke who didn't check a sum and—
